title: User-Controllable Hierarchical Memory System for Personal AI Assistants
abstract: Current AI assistants and large language models suffer from two critical limitations: short context window and lack of user control over memory. These issues lead to poor long-term user experience and serious privacy concerns. title: BrainBox: Hebbian Memory Architecture for AI Coding Agents
abstract: We present BrainBox, a novel memory architecture for AI coding agents that learns behavioral patterns using Hebbian learning and synaptic myelination. Unlike declarative memory systems (Mem0, SuperMemory, OpenMemory, Zep, Letta, LangMem), BrainBox implements procedural memory — learning how agents work rather than what they know.

title: Git-Native Agent Memory (GAM): A Verifiable Foundation for AI Cognitive Continuity
abstract: This paper introduces Git-Native Agent Memory (GAM), a memory architecture that leverages git's version control primitives to provide cryptographically verifiable, human-auditable, temporally-aware agent memory. title: A Hybrid, Multi-Layered Memory Architecture for Collaborative Reasoning in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: While Large Language Model (LLM) based multi-agent systems (MAS) show promise, their capabilities are constrained by simplistic, monolithic memory models. To address this, we propose a novel, four-tier hierarchical memory architecture inspired by cognitive science. Procedural Memory for Persistent LLM Agents: Know-How as the Missing Component
abstract: Persistent LLM agents currently possess episodic and semantic memory, but lack procedural memory—know-how, internalized procedures. abstract: Current AI assistants suffer from a fundamental asymmetry: users invest years of conversation, yet the AI retains no lasting understanding of who they are. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) stores utterances but does not distill them into structured knowledge. abstract: This study focuses on the tendency of agents in long-horizon sequential tasks to rely on short-term states and to underutilize historical information, and proposes a cognitive modeling and learning framework with long-term memory and reasoning capabilities. title: Markdown-Native Agent Memory and Skill Retrieval with FAISS: Building Persistent AI Systems without a Traditional Database
abstract: This paper presents a practical architecture for persistent AI assistants in which long-term memory, skill metadata, and agent operating context are stored as ordinary Markdown files rather than rows in a relational, document, or vector database. abstract: AI coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) currently access a narrow fraction of their training data—the technical vocabulary of programming—while ignoring the vast majority: literature, nature writing, navigation, warfare, poetry, and the full breadth of human sensory and emotional experience. abstract: Most AI memory systems treat all stored content equally. Importance may vary but the decay mechanics are uniform. title: Stratified Context System: A Query-Type-Aware Architecture for AI Agent Memory
abstract: We present the Stratified Context System (SCS), a novel architecture for AI agent memory that addresses the fundamental limitation of existing approaches: the assumption that a single storage mechanism can serve all retrieval modalities. abstract: Multi-agent AI systems suffer from goal drift, cascading errors, memory poisoning, and context window dependency.
